model: Life insurer FCFE at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case five-year average revenue growth: FY2026 premium guidance 6.5-7.0% decelerating toward the 4.7-4.8% historical revenue CAGR and 2.5% terminal
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: GAAP equity CAGRs are meaningless for GL: the LDTI adoption restated FY2021 equity to $2.0bn from $8.8bn and AOCI swings with rates, so the 3yr +14.8% and 5yr -7.4% equity CAGRs diverge from revenue (+4.7-4.8%) and EPS (+15.7-16.1%) by far more than 30%. EPS CAGR is buyback-inflated (share count 113M FY2020 -> 78M). Growth was selected from premium guidance and revenue history, not equity.
historical_growth.notes: fcf_3yr_cagr is on organic FCFE (dividends from subsidiaries ex-extraordinary less parent interest and expenses): ~$360M FY2022 -> ~$575M FY2025. fcf_5yr_cagr is null because FY2020 FCFE (~$180M, debt pre-funding and COVID capital retention) is not a comparable base. Reported FCF (OCF less capex, $1.25-1.43bn) is an insurer's operating cash flow and is not the owner series; it was not used for any CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: GL keeps doing what it has done for a decade: mid-single-digit premium growth from captive agencies and Medicare Supplement, a pre-tax margin in the mid-20s lifted slowly by reinvestment yields, roughly half of net operating income converted to excess cash at the parent and returned through repurchases. The class action is a cost, not a solvency event. Value is the FCFE stream at a 9% cost of equity; the stream, not GAAP book value, is what shareholders own.
scenario_narratives.bull: Agent-count growth and Medicare Supplement push premium growth to 7-7.5% for several years, net investment income re-rates the margin toward 26%, the litigation overhang clears cheaply, and statutory capital generation lets the parent take a larger share of earnings. Even here the model caps the exit at 16x FCFE: GL is a mature insurer, not a growth compounder.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2024 short-seller allegations were a preview of the model's structural weakness -- an independent-contractor sales force selling to an economically fragile demographic. A recession lifts lapses, a settlement and market-conduct scrutiny slow recruiting, health claims keep inflating, and premium growth fades to 2% with margins compressing toward 21.5%. Capital is trapped in the subsidiaries; buybacks slow; the stock de-rates to a low-teens FCFE multiple.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Globe Life is valued as the present value of the free cash flow to equity its holding company can actually extract -- dividends from the insurance subsidiaries after statutory capital retention, parent interest and expenses -- discounted at a 9% cost of equity, with no separate net-debt deduction because the holdco debt is serviced inside the flows. GAAP book value was rejected as the compounding base (LDTI/AOCI distortions) but serves as a cross-check: book value per share ex-AOCI was $100.04 at 30 June 2026 growing ~11%/yr; at a 1.5x exit P/B on year-5 BVPS-ex-AOCI (~$168) discounted at 9%, plus dividends, the cross-check lands around $170, above the FCFE base case, which tells the reader the market price (~1.67x BVPS ex-AOCI, ~10.6x FY2026 guided NOI of $15.55-15.95) is capitalising the leverage-funded and option-proceeds-funded portion of GL's buybacks, which this model deliberately does not credit. The terminal is capped at 15x FCFE in base (12x bear, 16x bull).
key_risks_to_valuation: Capital-retention assumption (capex_pct 10% -> 7.5% of revenue) is the single most important driver: every 1pp of revenue retained permanently is ~$9-10/share; it is calibrated to FY2023-25 organic excess cash flow, which ranged 6.1-9.6% of revenue
Securities class action (E.D. Texas, 4:24-cv-00376) and derivative suit: a large settlement is a bear-case cost, not modelled in base beyond ongoing legal expense inside the margin
Cash tax rate ramps from 14% to 20%; if the DAC/reserve timing shelter persists (taxes paid were 9.8% of pre-tax in FY2025) the base case is ~$8-10/share too low
Pre-tax margin path excludes the Q3 annual assumption-update remeasurement gains that lifted FY2024-25 to 23.7-24.9%; if those recur the base is conservative by ~1pp of margin
Rates: a lower-for-longer cycle would compress the net-investment-income tailwind assumed in the margin drift; the $1.6bn AOCI unrealised loss does not affect the FCFE stream unless bonds are sold
Recession sensitivity of the middle/lower-income policyholder base (lapse rates) and health-claim inflation at United American drive the bear-case margin and growth paths

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 127.85-191.55
data_sources.financials: GL_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, FY2006-Q2 2026); Q2 2026 10-Q (gl-20260630.htm, filed 2026-08-05) for cover share count, dilutive options, H1-2026 pre-tax income, interest expense, debt issuance, repurchases and BVPS ex-AOCI; FY2025 10-K (gl-20251231.htm, filed 2026-02-25) for pre-tax income, income taxes paid, interest expense, dividends from subsidiaries, extraordinary dividends and RBC ratio
data_sources.qualitative: GL_Analysis.json (2026-09-28): guidance FY2026 NOI $15.55-15.95/diluted share, premium growth 6.5-7%, life underwriting margin 42-44%, RBC target 300-320%, $2.5bn repurchase authorisation Aug-2026

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement add-back ($53.4M); GL publishes no combined equity-award-tax figure, and option exercises fund anti-dilutive repurchases (proceeds $164.4M in 2025) which are excluded from both SBC and buyback_cash
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases from excess cash flow $685M (5.4M shares at $126.41); total financing-line repurchases $881M include ~$196M anti-dilutive buys funded by option-exercise proceeds. H1-2026: $378M / 2.6M shares at $146.99 from excess cash flow.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API; no newer print on 2026-09-28)
inputs.share_count_basis: 76,849,447 common shares outstanding at July 31, 2026 (Q2 2026 10-Q cover) plus 1.45M weighted-average dilutive options (Q2 2026 EPS note) = 78.3M fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows and GL repurchases the option-exercise shares with the exercise proceeds (charged once). The Metrics.csv SharesOutstanding column (92.2M for FY2025-Q2 2026) is a stale carried-forward figure and was not used.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 9.0% for a USD-denominated US life/supplemental-health insurer: 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.95, rounded. This is a cost of EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flows are post-interest FCFE (parent interest expense $141M in FY2025 is inside the pre-tax margin). Same rate in all three scenarios; risk is carried in the driver paths and the probability weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: operating leases immaterial for an insurer; no lease adjustment in flows or bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: no minority interests in consolidated subsidiaries.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO. Holdco debt of $2,665.3M at 30 June 2026 (up $350M on a Q2-2026 issuance) is serviced inside the flows (interest expense inside the pre-tax margin); deducting it again after capitalising a post-interest stream would count it twice. Investment-portfolio assets and policy reserves are operating items, not net cash or net debt.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity on a life insurer, run through the owner-FCF component engine with net debt at zero (the IAG.AX / GMG.AX / CHC.AX cost-of-equity-stream precedent). Routing table default for an insurer is BVPS-compounding x exit P/B; overridden because (1) GAAP equity is not a usable compounding base -- the LDTI restatement took reported equity from $8.8bn (FY2020) to $2.0bn (FY2021 restated) and a $1.6bn AOCI unrealised-loss position moves it with rates, and (2) GL does not compound book: it distributes essentially all excess statutory capital via repurchases ($11.4bn since 1986), so the value driver is the parent's excess cash flow, i.e. FCFE. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total revenue (premium + net investment income + other); ebitda_margin_path = pre-tax income BEFORE stock compensation as % of revenue (FY2025 24.85% incl. Q3 assumption-update gains; FY2024 23.65%; FY2023 22.5%; H1-2026 22.8% -- H1 run-rates exclude the Q3 remeasurement gains, so year-1 base 23.75% sits between); sbc_pct_path charges SBC (0.9% of revenue); da_pct_path = 0 (D&A immaterial; capex is not PP&E here); capex_pct_path = statutory capital RETAINED in the insurance subsidiaries (RBC 300-320% target, 316% at FY2025, plus statutory new-business strain), calibrated so year-1 FCFE ~$610M ties to the organic excess cash flow (dividends from subsidiaries $815.7M in FY2025 less $80M extraordinary, less $141M parent interest and ~$20M parent expenses = ~$575M; 2023 ~$340M and 2024 ~$355M on the same basis; management says 2026 excess cash flows will be below 2025's, which carried $272M of extraordinary dividends), and tapering as growth slows because the RBC-growth component scales with growth; cash_tax_rate_path ramps from near the cash rate (taxes paid $140.9M = 9.8% of pre-tax in FY2025, vs 19.1% book, on DAC/reserve timing differences) toward the ~20% book rate rather than perpetuating the shelter. last_fcf is the FY2025 organic FCFE (~$575M), NOT reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income: an insurer's OCF-less-capex ($1,253.9M) is not free cash, so that identity is deliberately not satisfied here. The Q2-2026 cover share count is used with dilutive options; the CSV's 92.2M is stale.

bear.narrative: A recession lifts lapses in the working-class book and DTC channel, sales-practice litigation and a state market-conduct cycle slow agent recruiting so premium growth fades to 2%, health-claim utilisation keeps compressing United American's margin, the securities class action costs a nine-figure settlement plus legal expense (pre-tax margin drifts to 21.5%), and regulators keep more capital in the subsidiaries (retention ~9-10.5% of revenue); terminal growth 2.0%, cap 12x.

base.narrative: Premium growth follows FY2026 guidance (6.5-7%) then decelerates to 2.5% as the exclusive-agency count matures toward the ~28,000 goal and Medicare Supplement growth normalises; pre-SBC pre-tax margin drifts from 23.75% to 24.5% on net-investment-income reinvestment tailwind partly offset by health-claim inflation; capital retention tapers from 10% to 7.5% of revenue as the RBC-growth need shrinks; cash tax ramps to the 20% book rate; terminal at min(Gordon 9%/2.5%, 15x FCFE).

bull.narrative: Agent recruiting keeps compounding (double-digit producing-agent growth at American Income and Liberty National), Medicare Supplement keeps health premium growing double digits, new-money yields lift the pre-tax margin to 26%, the class action settles for an immaterial sum, and statutory capital generation lets retention fall to 6.5% of revenue; terminal growth 3.0%, cap 16x.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the securities class action survived its motion to dismiss (Sept 2025) and the derivative suit is live, and the captive independent-contractor sales model is a recurring source of allegation risk. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to hold at once -- sustained agent growth, the NII re-rating, health-claim normalisation and a cheap litigation exit. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
